ch15_ex3_q1: Estimate: $80^\circ$ is close to $90^\circ$, so $c$ should be a little under the Pythagoras value $\sqrt{3.4^2 + 7.8^2} \approx 8.5$.
Link: when $C = 90^\circ$, $\cos(C) = 0$ and the cosine rule becomes Pythagoras' theorem.
ch15_ex3_q2: Sense check: $A$ is slightly less than $60^\circ$. At exactly $60^\circ$ the rule becomes $a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - bc$, giving about 56.2, so $a$ should be a bit under 56.
ch15_ex3_q3: Obtuse test: $B$ is obtuse exactly when $b^2 > a^2 + c^2$. Here $532.7 > 389$, which confirms $b$ is the longest side.
After finding $b$, any remaining angle is safe to find with the sine rule, because a triangle with an obtuse angle cannot have another one.
ch15_ex3_q4: Scaling shortcut: sides 4, 6, 8 are $2 \times (2, 3, 4)$, and scaling does not change angles. So $\cos(A) = \frac{9 + 16 - 4}{2 \times 3 \times 4} = \frac{21}{24} = \frac{7}{8}$.
With whole-number sides the cosine is an exact fraction; simplify it before using $\cos^{-1}$.
ch15_ex3_q5: Quick obtuse test: compare $a^2 = 126\,736$ with $b^2 + c^2 = 130\,465$. It is slightly smaller, so the largest angle is acute but close to $90^\circ$.
ch15_ex3_q6: Find the largest angle ($C$, opposite 26.4) with the cosine rule first. Then the other two must be acute, so the sine rule can find them with no ambiguity.
Since $26.4^2 = 696.96 < 23.6^2 + 17.3^2 = 856.25$, the triangle has no obtuse angle.
ch15_ex3_q7: Work in kilometres to keep numbers small: $d^2 = 1.5^2 + 1.2^2 - 2(1.5)(1.2)\cos(110^\circ) \approx 4.92$, so $d \approx 2.218$ km $= 2218$ m.
ch15_ex3_q8a: Coordinate check: east $= -12\sin(68^\circ) + 7\sin(34^\circ) \approx -7.21$, north $= 12\cos(68^\circ) + 7\cos(34^\circ) \approx 10.30$. Distance $= \sqrt{7.21^2 + 10.30^2} \approx 12.57$ km.
ch15_ex3_q8b: Shortcut: find the bearing of F from S first (about N$35^\circ$W), then reverse it by swapping N/S and E/W to get S$35^\circ$E.
ch15_ex3_q9a: Check the type of triangle: $5.2^2 = 27.04 < 3^2 + 4.5^2 = 29.25$, so every angle is acute.
ch15_ex3_q9b: The area formula works with any angle: choose the angle you already know and multiply the two sides that form it.
ch15_ex3_q10: Sense check: the goal mouth (3 m) is the shortest side, so the angle opposite it is the smallest angle and must be under $60^\circ$.
ch15_ex3_q11: Alternative route: find the area with Heron's formula ($s = 127.5$, area $\approx 1559.6\text{ m}^2$), then height $= \frac{2 \times \text{area}}{\text{base}} = \frac{2 \times 1559.6}{35} \approx 89.12$ m.
ch15_ex3_q12a: With $60^\circ$, $\cos(60^\circ) = \frac{1}{2}$ turns the rule into $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - ab$, so everything stays whole: $6400 + 22\,500 - 12\,000 = 16\,900$.
Scaling shortcut: 80, 150 and 130 are $10 \times (8, 15, 13)$, a whole-number triangle with a $60^\circ$ angle.
ch15_ex3_q12b: Use the scaled triangle 8, 13, 15: $\cos(O) = \frac{64 + 169 - 225}{2 \times 8 \times 13} = \frac{8}{208} = \frac{1}{26}$, an exact value.
ch15_ex3_q13: Sense check: $AB$ must be between $31.6 - 16.2 = 15.4$ km and $47.8$ km. The $64^\circ$ angle is less than $90^\circ$, so $AB$ is also below $\sqrt{16.2^2 + 31.6^2} \approx 35.5$ km.
ch15_ex3_q14: If the difference between two true bearings is more than $180^\circ$, subtract it from $360^\circ$ to get the angle inside the triangle.
The included angle $135^\circ$ is obtuse, so the distance must be more than $\sqrt{50^2 + 30^2} \approx 58.3$ km.
ch15_ex3_q15: Since $14^2 = 196 < 11^2 + 13^2 = 290$, even the largest angle is acute, so the answer must be below $90^\circ$.
ch15_ex3_q16a: With $60^\circ$ the rule simplifies to $d^2 = p^2 + q^2 - pq = 49 + 100 - 70 = 79$, with no calculator needed.
ch15_ex3_q16b: Exact form: $\cos(B) = \frac{28}{14\sqrt{79}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{79}}$, which avoids any rounding of the diagonal.
ch15_ex3_q16c: Calculator technique: keep $B$ in memory, then type $150 - \text{Ans}$ to get the upper included angle without retyping a rounded value.
ch15_ex3_q17: Angles of depression from the cliff top equal the angles of elevation from the yacht (alternate angles), so you can work in the right-angled triangles at sea level.
10 minutes is $\frac{1}{6}$ h, so multiply the distance in km by 6 to get km/h.
ch15_ex3_q18: Quick angle-type check: $AC^2 = 89$ is less than $AB^2 + BC^2 = 97$, so angle $ABC$ is acute but close to $90^\circ$.
Face diagonals of a box are just Pythagoras on each face: length², width² and height² pair up in twos.
ch15_ex3_q19b: From part (a), $AB^2 + BC^2 - AC^2 = 2DB^2$, so $\cos(\angle ABC) = \frac{DB^2}{AB \times BC} = \frac{13.69}{24.44} \approx 0.5601$.
